title: Projective level parameter schemes for stable pointed curves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $g\geq2$ and $n\geq0$ integers. There exist a finite-type projective $k$-scheme $M$ and a family with ordered sections $(\mathcal U\to M,t_1,\ldots,t_n)$ having these properties.

(a) For every $k$-scheme $B$ and every $k$-morphism $m:B\to M$, the pullback $(\mathcal U\times_M B\to B,t_{1,B},\ldots,t_{n,B})$ is a stable pointed curve; projectivity here is allowed in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism].

(b) Let $F/k$ be any field extension and let $(C,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral $F$-curve of genus $g$ with distinct $F$-rational markings. The functor on $F$-schemes $B$ whose elements are pairs $(m,\alpha)$, where $m:B\to M$ is a $k$-morphism and $\alpha:(\mathcal U\times_M B,t_{1,B},\ldots,t_{n,B})\xrightarrow{\sim}(C\times_F B,p_{1,B},\ldots,p_{n,B})$ is an isomorphism preserving each labelled section, is represented by a nonempty finite etale $F$-scheme $P_C$. Represented means that these pairs are naturally in bijection with $F$-morphisms $B\to P_C$.

A stable pointed curve over a scheme $T$ means a projective flat finitely presented family with nonempty connected reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one, whose only singularities are ordinary double points, together with finitely many disjoint sections in its relative smooth locus. On the normalization of each irreducible component of every geometric fibre, a component of genus zero has at least three special points and one of genus one has at least one; special points are inverse images of nodes or markings. An ordinary double point has completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. The marking may be empty. A genus is computed on the smooth projective normalization of a geometric component. The markings are unordered when isomorphisms are allowed to permute them.

Fields, field extensions, schemes, finite type, projectivity of $M$ and $C$, geometric integrality, smoothness, finite morphisms, etaleness, fibre products and genus use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-pc-genus]. In the stable-family condition, flatness, finite presentation, geometric fibres, dimension, normalization, completion and formal power series use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].

proof.text: Choose $\ell=3$ if $\operatorname{char}(k)\ne3$, and $\ell=5$ otherwise; it is a prime at least three invertible in $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-unpointed-level-normalization-projectivity]. It supplies $M_0=Z_{g,\ell}$, finite type and H-projective over $k$, its actual stable unpointed genus-$g$ family and map $a_0$, and the natural identification of its smooth-curve isomorphism fibres with finite etale surjective frame schemes. The full level cover, including all components, is used.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-pointed-universal-curve-tower] to this $M_0,a_0$ and $n$. Set $M=T_n$ and take the stable ordered family specified by $a_n$. The lemma gives a finite-type H-projective $M$, the iterated 2-cartesian forgetful squares, and stability of the family after every base change $B\to M$. Its bundle-projectivity conclusion is precisely the convention allowed in (a). This proves (a), including $n=0$.

Projectivity conversion uses Stacks Tags 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective) and 01WE (lemma-H-projective-composition). proof.text: For $F/k$ and $(C,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ in (b), apply [lem-sfb-smooth-marking-isomorphism-fibre-comparison] to the tower. Its hypotheses hold by Step 2, and geometric integrality implies geometric connectedness. It gives a natural bijection from the required labelled pairs $(m,\alpha)$ to unpointed pairs $(m_0,\beta)$ over $M_0$. The frame-fibre assertion of [lem-sfb-unpointed-level-normalization-projectivity] represents the latter functor by a finite etale surjective $F$-scheme $P_C$. Composing the two natural bijections proves representability on all $F$-schemes, with the isomorphism and every label retained. Surjectivity over the nonempty $\operatorname{Spec}F$ gives $P_C\ne\varnothing$; an $F$-rational frame is unnecessary. This proves (b).
